# Local alphaTab patches

Pinned build: alphaTab 1.8.4 (MPL-2.0, see `LICENSE` and `LICENSE.header`). Only `alphaTab.js` is modified; every other alphaTab file matches the npm release `@coderline/alphatab@1.8.4`. The exact changes are in `alphaTab-1.8.4-fretlark.patch`, a unified diff against that release's `dist/alphaTab.js`, so the modified source is available under MPL-2.0.

- `alphaTab.js`, `AlphaSynthWebWorkerApi.loadedMidiInfo`: return `_loadedMidiInfo` instead of recursively reading `loadedMidiInfo`. The public `midiLoaded.on()` event reads this getter on registration; the recursive getter overflows the stack and prevents editor startup. `verify-editor-refresh.cjs` checks the getter against its backing value. Recheck this patch when replacing the bundled build.
- `alphaTab.js`, `GpifWriter._writeSoundsAndAutomations` and `GpifParser._parseAutomation`: write and read per-bar track `Volume` and `Pan` automations (Guitar Pro stores 0..1; alphaTab uses 0..16). Stock 1.8.4 plays these automations but drops them on GP export and import. `verify-automation.cjs` round-trips them. Recheck when replacing the bundled build.
- `alphaTab.js`, `AlphaSynthAudioWorkletOutput`: serialize worklet `play`/`pause`/`destroy` operations and abort pending module loads on destroy. Stock 1.8.4 starts asynchronous worklet setup for each `play()` without ordering it against `pause()`, so pausing during the (slower, first-load) count-in setup leaves a stale setup connected and can start a later play's source twice. Playback then reports Playing while the position and audio stay frozen. This ports the 1.9.0 lifecycle fix. `verify-playback.cjs` covers overlapping play/pause/play with delayed worklet loads. Recheck when replacing the bundled build.
- `alphaTab.js`, `AlphaSynth.timePosition` setter and `MidiFileSequencer.generateCountInMidi`: seeking while the count-in plays now ends the count-in first (stock 1.8.4 measured the new song position against the count-in clock and kept playing the stale count-in audio), and the count-in falls back to the song's first tempo, then 120 BPM and 4/4, when the synth reports no tempo or time signature (a zero tempo made an endless count-in). `verify-editor-refresh.cjs` checks the seek order. Recheck when replacing the bundled build.
